MILITARY_ENERGY_AUTONOMY.summary: The evidence indicates that the U.S. military is actively pursuing deployable autonomous power solutions—particularly nuclear microreactors and DC microgrids—at multiple installations, moving beyond pilot projects toward operational deployment.
trigger: The Department of the Air Force announced that it has selected three companies to potentially develop and operate a microreactor on a DAF installation, with Buckley Space Force Base, Colorado, and Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana chosen as the first two sites. (candidate_id: 03d50e0782d626fbdd6a)

A bid has been issued for the construction of a power generation system with a microgrid at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Hanover, NJ, including a 400 kW photovoltaic array, a 1.5 MW battery energy storage system, a microgrid controller, and two 500 kW natural‑gas generators. (candidate_id: db137d024859765037dd)

The first phase of a resilient DC microgrid project was brought online at Kirtland Air Force Base, consisting of a single‑bus, ten‑node 250 kW DC microgrid, marking the first such collaboration between the Department of Energy and a Department of Defense site. (candidate_id: 9652ee54f0739d6fe2a9)

The Department of Defense broke ground on the Project Pele transportable microreactor at Idaho National Laboratory, a project that could become one of the first advanced reactors to operate in the United States as early as 2026. (candidate_id: 5ace3a6872445f3754a8)
